name: @endur/shared
//exports: Two entry points, chosen by who is asking. Everything that compiles TypeScript itself (tsx in dev, Vite, Vitest, tsc) takes `default` and reads src/, so an edit here is live on the next request and a fresh clone needs no build step. Plain `node` cannot run src/ (its relative imports are written ./foo.js and no sibling .js exists there), so the production start passes --conditions=compiled and gets dist/. Pointing `default` at dist/ instead made every dev server and test run read whatever dist/ was last built: on 2026-10-16 that was a 1 Sep build with no `trial` on RegisterBody, so Zod stripped it and every trial sign-up was treated as a paid one.
